title: Why is the sea salty?
examples: Where does all the salt in the ocean come from?
Does salt just fall from the sky into the sea?
If the water evaporates, where does the salt go?

explain.say: Some rivers carry salt from the rocks they flow past.
The salt dissolves in the fresh river water.
When the sun heats the water, it turns into gas.

draw.text: Sun heats water, turns to gas.

explain.say: This process is called evaporation, and it leaves salt behind.
So, rivers bring salt, and the sun helps leave it in the sea.

draw.text: Rivers bring salt; sun leaves it.

explain.say: When you see puddles drying up on a sunny day, the water goes up.

draw.text: Puddles dry up in the sun.

faq.a: Rivers carry salt from rocks into the sea. The sun then evaporates the water, leaving the salt behind.
asks: Where does the salt in the ocean come from?
How does salt get into the sea?

faq.q: Does the salt just float in the river?
faq.a: No, the salt dissolves completely into the water, making the water salty.
asks: Does salt mix with river water?
Can salt mix with fresh water?

faq.q: What happens to the salt when the water evaporates?
faq.a: The water turns into invisible gas and goes up. The salt cannot turn into gas, so it stays behind.
asks: Does salt disappear when water evaporates?
Where does the salt go after evaporation?

faq.a: Most rivers are fresh, but they can pick up salt from rocks or other sources.
asks: Can rivers have salt in them?

faq.q: Is the salt in the sea always the same?
faq.a: The amount of salt can change slowly over a very long time.
asks: Does the sea level affect the saltiness?

facts: Rivers carry minerals and salt from the rocks they flow over.
Evaporation is the process where liquid turns into water vapor.
The salt remains behind when the water evaporates.
The ocean is much saltier than most rivers.

quiz.say: Rivers carry salt from which source?
quiz.why: Rivers flow over rocks, and the salt from those rocks dissolves into the water.

wrong.0: Wind moves things, but it does not carry dissolved salt from rocks.
wrong.2: The sky brings rain, but the salt comes from the land.
wrong.3: The sea is already salty; the source must be before it reaches the sea.

quiz.say: What process leaves salt behind in the sea?
quiz.why: Evaporation turns water into gas, leaving the solid salt crystals behind.

wrong.0: Dissolving mixes salt and water, but it does not remove the water.
wrong.1: Flowing moves water, but it does not change the state of the water.
wrong.2: Freezing makes ice, which keeps the salt mixed in the ice.

quiz.say: If a river flows into the ocean, what is the main source of the salt?
quiz.why: The river is the pathway that brings the dissolved salt from the land to the ocean.

wrong.1: This is circular thinking; the ocean is the destination, not the source.
wrong.2: Rain usually falls as fresh water, not carrying rock salt.
wrong.3: The sun's heat causes evaporation, it does not introduce salt.
